scenes: ten point five million Australian dollars. Sent by mistake. It was supposed to be a one hundred dollar refund.
May twenty twenty-one. Crypto.com, the company that paid seven hundred million dollars to put its name on an arena in Los Angeles, owes an Australian woman a small refund. About one hundred dollars.
An employee types her account number, into the amount box.
ten point four seven million dollars lands in her account. And nobody notices.
Not for a day. Not for a week. For seven months.
In December, an audit finally finds the hole.
But the money has already moved. A five-bedroom house in Melbourne. one point three five million dollars. Bought for her sister.
Crypto.com takes her to court. The judge orders the house sold.
And the money goes back. With interest. One wrong box. Ten million dollars.
Money sent to you by mistake is never yours. It always comes back for you. Follow Chain Secrets.
